- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and forecast is above recent high, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.  
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged negative sentiment — add 1–3% bias upward to reflect mean reversion toward prior range.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast by adding 0.5–1.5% per day lagged sentiment strength.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative — apply 1–2% upward bias to avoid underestimation.
